items.q: What should you remember about extreme co-design exists because distributed AI workloads hit Amdahl's Law?
items.a: **you must shard pipeline,** data, and model, making networking/CPU/memory/power all bottlenecks.

items.q: Why does this matter: Company org charts should mirror the product you build, not generic hamburger charts; Jensen has 60+ direct re?
items.a: **Company org charts should mirror the product** you build, not generic hamburger charts; Jensen has 60+ direct reports, almost all engineers.

items.q: What should you remember about **Install base defines architecture**?
items.a: **x86 survived despite elegance criticism;** CUDA on every GeForce built developer reach before cloud existed.

items.q: What should you remember about four scaling laws loop?
items.a: **agentic systems generate data → back to pre-training** → post-training → test-time → deploy; synthetic data is normal (most human teaching is synthetic too).

items.q: What should you remember about inference/thinking is harder than pre-training/memorization?
items.a: **test-time scaling is intensely** compute-heavy; agentic scaling multiplies AI like hiring employees.

items.q: What should you remember about aI model architectures change ~every 6 months; hardware ~every 3 years?
items.a: **NVIDIA does internal research** + listens to every AI lab + keeps CUDA flexible.

items.q: What should you remember about digital workers need file systems, research, and tools?
items.a: **OpenClaw schematic was at** GTC two years before launch; agents use microwaves, not finger-lasers.

items.q: Why does this matter: Token cost drops ~10×/year via perf/watt co-design; NVIDIA scaled compute ~1M× in 10 years vs Moore's Law ~100?
items.a: **Token cost drops ~10×/year via perf/watt** co-design; NVIDIA scaled compute ~1M× in 10 years vs Moore's Law ~100×.

items.q: What should you remember about supply chain?
items.a: **200 suppliers, 1.3M components per Vera Rubin** rack; Jensen informs upstream/downstream CEOs like employees — no contract with TSMC after decades.

items.q: What should you remember about power grid runs ~60% of peak 99% of the time?
items.a: **data centers should gracefully** degrade during rare peak demand instead of requiring six-nines.

items.q: What should you remember about elon's Colossus lesson?
items.a: **question necessity, method, timeline;** be present at point of action; personal urgency propagates.

items.q: What should you remember about nVIDIA moat #1?
items.a: **CUDA install base + developer trust; moat #2**: horizontal ecosystem integration across every industry/cloud.
